items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And Bolden was drafted. So they decided to make me the leader.

ctx.x: And while we were working this particular job... It was during the War. There was plenty of soldiers, we were near Camp Polk and everything was happening. And it gave me an opportunity to see Lips(?) Rose again, the great saxophone player, and his wife Edith Kirk(?), because they were stationed in Alexandria. So that was nice, to be around them again.

And Bolden was drafted. So they decided to make me the leader. I was voted the leader of the band! So we stayed there, and played until we were approached about another job in Tampa, Florida, at a place called Wat Sanders' Blue Room -- the Blue Room, and Wat Sanders was the guy who owned it. And so we decided to take it. So we went down there, and I stayed down there for about three months. And I had a great time. In fact, that's where I met one of the great pianists, one of the greatest pianists you would ever…
